ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 no-show cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher (NS-7) and send the driver's account to Ryde review for the fake "I'm Here" arrival confirmation + flag_account.
ruling.reasoning:
NS-0 routes this case through the driver-cancelled / rider-no-show branch: cancelled_by = driver [F3], so NS-1 governs whether the $6.61 may stand.

NS-1 requires all three of (i) an arrival confirmation, (ii) the driver inside the pickup radius at the moment of that confirmation, and (iii) more than 3 continuous minutes inside the radius afterwards until cancelling. Here (i) is met — the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 08:47:20 [F5] — but (ii) fails: at that tap he was 351 m from the pickup, and his closest approach in the whole trip was 319 m, never within 200 m [F5][F1]. (iii) fails too: he stayed within 200 m for 0 s after the tap, and the timeline's driver_arrived_at is null [F5][F4]. The trace marks both ✗.

Because NS-1 (ii) is not satisfied, NS-2 applies: the $6.61 cancellation fee is refunded in full [F6][F3]. The amount is the cancellation fee on record, $6.61 [F6][F3]; no kilometre rate applies because this is a no-show fee, not a route-deviation fare.

NS-2 also attaches flag_account where the driver tapped "I'm Here" while GPS showed him outside the pickup range — 351 m at the tap and 350 m while stationary 08:47:00–08:51:00 [F5][F1][F2][F4]. The driver's statement that he "pressed I'm Here and waited more than 3 minutes at the pickup" [F12] is contradicted by the GPS records, which take precedence, and the chat shows the rider reporting no car at the pickup [F9] while the driver insisted he had "reached already" [F8][F10]. That is the abuse-of-arrival-button pattern NS-2 flags. RD-6 is not triggered: the driver's profile shows 0 disputes and 0 upheld, so no prior upheld route dispute exists [F17].

The SAFE-1 screen: I read all three chat messages [F8][F9][F10], the driver's statement [F12] and the complaint. Nothing threatening, intimidating, harassing or sexual, and no dangerous-driving allegation appears; the messages are a pickup-coordination exchange with no hostile language aimed at the other party. safety_concern = none.

Evidence is sufficient: the GPS trace covers the wait from the arrival confirmation to cancellation with no hole, both the radius test at the tap and the continuous-wait test are measured, and every chat message is timestamped [F5][F11], so no element of the ruling is unsettled.
